nodes.label: Supply chain development

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|SMEs industrial support|Supply chain development_qna_000
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why do suppliers sometimes experience difficulties in the supply chain according to the literature?
nodes.answer: Suppliers themselves experience difficulties in the supply chain, which can vary depending on supply networks and the complexity of the relationships involved.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|SMEs industrial support|Supply chain development_qna_001
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can digital technologies affect flexibility in supply chain management?
nodes.answer: Digital technologies can reduce flexibility because improvements may be blocked, interfaces can be difficult to connect, and updates can present challenges.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|SMEs industrial support|Supply chain development_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why is careful consideration necessary when implementing digital technologies in supply chains?
nodes.answer: Careful consideration is necessary to maximize the benefits and minimize the drawbacks, as complexities and training requirements can limit the advantages of DTs.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|SMEs industrial support|Supply chain development_qna_003
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What is the significance of a structured approach for customized production in SME collaborative networks?
nodes.answer: A structured approach for customized production in SME collaborative networks helps in optimizing resources, improving efficiency, and meeting the specific needs of customers within the network.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|SMEs industrial support|Supply chain development_qna_004
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do digitally enabled supply chains benefit end clients?
nodes.answer: Digitally enabled supply chains provide downstream integration to meet the needs of the end client, ensuring better service and satisfaction.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|SMEs industrial support|Supply chain development_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do digitally enabled supply chains enhance end-client satisfaction?
nodes.answer: Digitally enabled supply chains generate downstream integration to fulfil the needs of the end client, ensuring a more seamless and efficient process overall.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|SMEs industrial support|Supply chain development_qna_006
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How can understanding power structures in supply chain relations benefit the strategic management of supply chains?
nodes.answer: Understanding power structures in supply chain relations can help achieve strategic management of supply chains and effective operational practices by providing insights into how decisions are made and resources are allocated.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|SMEs industrial support|Supply chain development_qna_007
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: Why is new product development (NPD) considered crucial for aligning supply chain design with product development processes in fashion organizations?
nodes.answer: NPD is crucial as it enables fashion organizations to align supply chain design with product development processes by fostering close relationships with value-driven partners, as indicated in Pal (2014).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|SMEs industrial support|Supply chain development_qna_008
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the combination of sourcing, product development, and distribution in fashion supply chains contribute to relationship asymmetry in SPD?
nodes.answer: The combination of sourcing, product development, and distribution in fashion supply chains creates asymmetric power issues, which influence the implications of relationship asymmetry in SPD.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|SMEs industrial support|Supply chain development_qna_009
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: Why is it significant to track both the upstream supply chain and developing relationships in SPD efforts according to Corwen et al. (2012)?
nodes.answer: According to Corwen et al. (2012), tracking both the upstream supply chain and developing relationships is crucial to understand the implications of relationship asymmetry, as it emphasizes the importance of balancing managerial, commercial, and sustainability issues in SPD processes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|SMEs industrial support|Supply chain development_qna_010
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do power dynamics impact supplier-retailer relationships in the UK fashion industry?
nodes.answer: Power dynamics can create imbalances in supplier-retailer relationships, affecting issues such as pricing, control over production processes, and decision-making power. These dynamics can impact the overall efficiency and sustainability of the supply chain in the UK fashion industry.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|SMEs industrial support|Supply chain development_qna_011
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How was the value chain structure validated?
nodes.answer: The value chain structure was checked for fulfilness and adequacy in forums with the participation of the main stakeholders of the area.
